problem.text: Model.get_storage_info recognized only the exact key lm_head. Gemma3's language_model.lm_head therefore entered the ordinary Linear totals, leaving reported head BPW at zero.

reasoning.text: The patch replaces equality with endswith("lm_head"), recognizing component-prefixed heads without changing model declarations or the accounting formulas.

impact.text: eval/ppl.py directly calls this method and prints its decoder/head bitrates. The comparison adapter has a separate helper already using suffix matching, so that helper is unchanged.

source_notes.text: An earlier entry describes the same suffix-recognition correction in the comparison adapter; this change applies it to the Model method.

Issue #6, “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr',” and #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” contain model.py import tracebacks. Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” contains a linear.py conversion traceback. Their shared paths are only an inferred contextual connection, not evidence that this accounting patch fixes those failures.

limitations: Validation used scalar accounting examples, not repository execution with loaded tensors or a GPU.
The storage estimate counts selected Linear tensors, not total runtime GPU memory. Model-level BPW values were not measured.

claims.text: Head classification precedes the general Linear branch. Matching a prefixed head now removes both its storage bits and weight count from the decoder average and assigns them to head accounting. Bare lm_head remains recognized.

Storage bits are eight times the sum of tensor element sizes in bytes multiplied by element counts. Linear.get_tensors delegates to its loaded inner implementation, or returns an empty dictionary when unloaded; weights_numel returns in_features × out_features. Thus BPW is storage per weight, not simply a configured quantization width.

A standard-library scalar transcription used 400 decoder bits over 100 weights and 320 head bits over 20 weights. For language_model.lm_head, the old/new results were (6, 0, 720) and (4, 16, 720): decoder BPW and head BPW change, while combined counted bits remain constant. The bare-head case remained (4, 16, 720).

Suffix matching is a lightweight naming convention rather than explicit head metadata: it accommodates language_model.lm_head but accepts any key ending in lm_head. The patch changes reporting classification, not quantization or forward computation.

annotation.summary: Corrects component-prefixed output-head BPW reporting by separating those heads from ordinary Linear storage totals.
